messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: GPU pool "cust-prod-a" hitting 100% utilization; queue length +420% vs baseline; autoscaler unable to add capacity (scale lock detected). incident severity: P1. link: https://monitoring.example/r/alert/2612345678
lia_oncall: I'm taking this. thanks for the ping. what region/pool? any customer-facing errors yet? :eyes:
sanjay: region: us-west-2, pool: gpu-cust-prod-a, reason field shows: autoscaler-lock:error=LeaseCooldownExceeded, batcher:drop_rate_up, prefix_cache_miss_rate spike. seeing a sudden >2x drop in effective throughput per-GPU starting 03:12 UTC.
lia_oncall: any recent deploys or config rollouts to batching/caching?
sanjay: yes — automated rollout from last night adjusted continuous-batching params and prefix cache TTLs: config commit 1d4f3 -> changed batch_window_ms from 30 -> 60 and prefix_cache_ttl from 300s -> 60s to reduce mem use. rollout 03:05 UTC across cust pools.
mike_serving: that TTL cut is likely culprit. more prefix cache misses => KV cache cold starts => higher per-request latencies => autoscaler sees higher queue but scaling is gated by lease cooldown. we also saw continuous-batcher holding onto in-flight sequences longer due to larger batch window causing head-of-line delays.
lia_oncall: customers? any 5xx or client visible throttles?
ops_pager: some customers reported elevated latencies and rate-limited responses; spike in 429s from gateway around 03:20-03:35. top impacted: AcmeHealth (prod), FinchSearch (staging->prod broad rollout).
sanjay: metrics quick dump: 
```
metric: queue_length: 420% up
metric: gpu_util: 98-100%
metric: prefix_cache_hit: 0.12 -> 0.02
metric: avg_token_latency_gpu: 90ms -> 220ms
metric: autoscaler_add_attempts: 12 failed (LeaseCooldownExceeded)
```
lia_oncall: ok. immediate mitigation options? enumerate short steps.
sanjay: 1) rollback batch_window & prefix_cache_ttl to last-known-good (commit a9c2b) — fastest. 2) temporarily override autoscaler cooldown to allow immediate scale-up (risky). 3) manually add an extra GPU node to pool (fastest, avoid autoscaler). 4) reduce batch size on serving tier to flush queue (degrades throughput but reduces latency).
mike_serving: priority is customer latency/availability. I'd prefer rollback + manual scale. rollback should restore cache hit rates quickly.
lia_oncall: executing rollback to a9c2b now. will also open manual node add request. tagging @kelly for node provisioning.
kelly: on it — requesting 2x GPU instances (g4-large equivalent) to be attached to gpu-cust-prod-a. ETA ~7-9 minutes.
lia_oncall: rollback command (infra-runner):
```
infractl config rollback --pool gpu-cust-prod-a --to-commit a9c2b --force-apply
```
lia_oncall: running rollback...
infra-bot: config rollback started by lia_oncall; job id jb-77823; applying to pool gpu-cust-prod-a.
sanjay: while rollback proceeds, temporarily bump autoscaler lease cooldown to 30s:
```
autoscalerctl set-config --pool gpu-cust-prod-a --lease-cooldown 30
```
lia_oncall: applied cooldown bump. note: we are lowering safety margin. monitoring closely.
ops_pager: provisioning update: nodes requested; cloud-req id cr-3321; will attach when config drift resolved.
kelly: nodes provisioned and attached at 03:28 UTC.
sanjay: rollback complete at 03:30 UTC per infra-bot. prefix_cache_ttl restored to 300s, batch_window_ms set back to 30. infra-bot logs show config apply OK.
infra-bot: config rollback jb-77823 completed successfully.
mike_serving: seeing prefix_cache_hit start climbing back: 0.02 -> 0.45 at 03:33; avg_token_latency_gpu falling to ~110ms. queue shrinking.
lia_oncall: queue length down ~60% from peak. autoscaler lock still occasionally failing but manual nodes + cooldown override gave headroom.
ops_pager: customer impact window noted: 03:12–03:35 UTC. notified AcmeHealth SRE; they confirmed transient errors but no data loss.
lia_oncall: raising temporary incident page to customer success to prepare PR message. tagging @ops_pager for timeline.
ops_pager: drafting message. will include mitigation steps and ETA for full verification.
kelly: rolling back the batch config also fixed a hot shard eviction noise we saw in logs. eviction counts decreased 90%.
sanjay: next steps: revert the automated rollout pipeline to block this config until we complete a targeted test plan. root cause hypothesis: TTL reduction caused prefix cache churn across hot keys; batch_window increase created larger batches that increased variance in in-flight sequence lengths causing KV cache thrashing + autoscaler lease contention.
lia_oncall: agreed. I'll keep this thread open until we've confirmed stability across 1 hour. assign postmortem owner? @mike_serving can you lead, with @sanjay and @kelly?
mike_serving: happy to. will set postmortem doc and invite infra, oncall, and devex.
lia_oncall: handoff to night oncall @kelly at 03:45 UTC — brief: rollback completed, nodes attached, ongoing monitoring for autoscaler lock events. contact list: lia_oncall, kelly, sanjay, mike_serving.
kelly: acknowledged. I'll watch the dashboards and escalate if queue rebound >20% for 15m.
ops_pager: customer note sent at 03:50 UTC; support triage open.
infra-bot: autoscaler lock events decreased to baseline at 04:01 UTC; closing automated alert.
lia_oncall: closing incident thread at 04:05 UTC; follow-up postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 UTC. action items: (1) block TTL change in pipeline until test harness for prefix_cache hit regressions exists, (2) add autoscaler safety override runbook, (3) add preflight that simulates batch_window increases against hot-key traffic.
mike_serving: creating postmortem doc now. will link here when ready. :spiral_notepad:
ops_pager: final note: total customer impact window ~23 min, P1 -> downgraded to P2 after mitigation.
kelly: thanks team. good coordination. :thumbsup:
